response: Yes, perspective-taking has been shown to increase patient satisfaction in medical encounters. When healthcare providers take the time to understand and acknowledge their patients' thoughts, feelings, and concerns, patients tend to feel more heard, validated, and empowered. This, in turn, can lead to higher patient satisfaction ratings, improved adherence to treatment plans, and better health outcomes. By actively listening to and empathizing with their patients, healthcare providers can build trust, strengthen the patient-provider relationship, and ultimately enhance the overall quality of care.
